profile.headline: PhD and Senior Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Driven by challenge and curiosity.  I combine an artist's creativity with a scientist's logical approach to solve software engineering problems.  Any complex system interests me, from neuroscience to warehouse inventory management.

I’m passionate about reducing friction in dev ex, improving cross-team collaboration, and up-skilling developers.  As a developer, my focus is building stable product by reducing code debt, improving testing methods, and implementing better architectural design.

As a team lead, my values are:
- Respect: there is no team without it.
- Seek Excellence: that is how we best serve ourselves and our customers.
- Teach Excellence: knowledge silos are dead-ends.
- Laugh: we work too hard not to.

positions.title: Senior Software Developer
positions.description:
Continuing my role as the lead developer for outbound team.  Half my time is spent coding and the rest of my time is spent:
- Reviewing code and discussing how to architect our product (e.g., on the four-dev architectural Review board)
- Helping my teammates reach the next step in their careers (e.g. running developer bookclub, holding regular 1:1s)
- Setting and maintaining a team culture of respect, transparency, diligence, and intentional growth
- Getting everything I know documented and/or recorded as presentations
- Discussing how to implement process improvements with my manager (and then doing it)
positions.insights: Software Design, Team Leadership and +1 skill

positions.title: Software Developer II
positions.description:
Leadership
- Dev lead for the Outbound Warehousing team (which is actually 2 teams in 1)
- Mentoring Summer Interns, 2023
- Scheduler and standby discussion leader for dev bookclub

Documentation Efforts: 
- Pick Planner: starts with high level concepts for support and new team members and dives into the deep details of specific processes for our new architecture.  Includes lots of flowcharts and diagrams.
- Currently expanding our documentation on Pick Order, a function my team did not develop, but inherited.  Focused on explaining its event-driven architecture, as the team is more familiar with transaction-driven architecture.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
- Integration Testing Framework: Co-designed and implemented the MVP for our integration testing framework for suitescript code in the NetSuite ERP.  The framework parses environment requirements for each test and ensures a NetSuite account exists that can provide that environment.  Compatible tests are grouped together, and the group is given a list of accounts it is compatible with.  Using puppeteer, we log into an available, compatible account and toggle features to match the test group's environment.  The grouped tests are then run on the account through the Integration Testing Suitelet (our API gateway).  Tests written in Jest.  Also presented the framework to QA and our Dev team and wrote the documentation for...
   - the framework code
   - installation
   - getting started writing integration tests in our framework
   - what should be ingratiation tested vs unit tested vs end-to-end tested

- Enhancing "Script Lock" Behavior and Recovery: To prevent duplicate batch processing, I added a new type of "script lock" to prevent a processor from using a batch record claimed by another processor.  To solve issues with an existing script lock type getting "stuck" and blocking most processing, I added more extensive checking to ensure locks were deleted after errors during processing or if a NetSuite server restarts.  Also, added a fallback mechanism to clear locks if an unexpected error occurred during normal, post-processing teardown.  At the end of each execution, I added a log reporting which parts of the tear down process were attempted and whether they succeeded in the normal teardown process or if the fallback logic was used.

- Unit Testing Guide: Included help on: test-driven-design, what to unit test, understanding how spies work, and common patterns to solve unit testing problems.  Sent out a PowerPoint with tips on how to unit test faster and make better tests and hosted a discussion on standard practices.
positions.insights: Domain-Driven Design (DDD), Software Documentation and +3 skills

positions.title: Programming Consultant
positions.description: Using an iterative, mockup process, completed an extensive redesign of TrustiPhi’s flagship angular app to provide a consistent, intuitive user-experience.  Responsible for developing new features of the redesigned application including resolvers and unit tests.  Extended and improved base functionality as well as implementing changes to meet web accessibility standards.  As part of this project, wrote over 60 JIRA stories.

honors.title: High Altitude Award
honors.description:
“Since Cristina has joined RF-SMART family she has made a tremendous impact not only on the product but on her teammates as well. Cristina has a very logical and methodical way of thinking about how to approach problems and seems to always bring to light a better way of doing something. When customer challenges arise, she is a go-to for our product team, as her understanding of the product from a functional and technical perspective is excellent. She will challenge ideas in a very fruitful way, encouraging others to think differently about how we approach problems, and digs down to the root of an issue and doesn’t just solve what’s presented on the surface.  

No task is too big or small for Cristina, she is very ambitious and has recently helped clean up our QA Automation Backlog by reviewing PR’s put out by that team. […]  She has recently been working on our prototype for our integration testing framework, which will enable our product to integrate directly into NetSuite and test our scenarios even faster than using end to end tests. We could potentially see nightly runs that typically take anywhere from 8-10 hours be decreased dramatically with this effort. This effort will also enable us to shift left and have our integration tests be part of our definition of done, meaning integration tests would be in place before we ever go into a release!  

Not only has Cristina contributed to furthering our product from a technical standpoint but she reaches outside of her NS Product team “box” and influences other parts of the organization. She played a big part in our recruiting initiative this summer, creating a recruiting video […].  

[…] When an issue is brought up or a challenging situation, Cristina’s name is always top of mind for tackling it! We love having her on the team, and our product wouldn’t be in the same spot it is today without her contributions!  

[…]

Thanks Cristina, for being unique, awesome, and always up for a new challenge!”
honors.issuer: Issued by RF-SMART, Nominated by my Manager Myles Hattabaugh · Dec 2022
